transit:1.sentence: carries as many subway riders a year as Mexico City
transit:1.note: MTA 2025 subway ridership; Mexico City Metro's 2025 ridership, the agency's own year-end figure as reported by the Quadratin news agency (the agency's site was not reachable). Both count entries rather than journeys, so they are measured the same way. Mexico City's metro is the second busiest in the Americas after New York's.

transit:8.sentence: logs as many bike-share rides a year as Paris does on Vélib'
transit:8.caveat: Paris's figure is a year behind.
transit:8.note: Lyft's March 2026 post on Citi Bike operations ('more than 46 million rides in 2025'); Vélib' trips in 2024 as reported by the French cycling trade site Cleanrider, because velib-metropole.fr blocks automated fetching. Vélib' is the older and larger-docked system; Citi Bike has more bikes.

transit:4.sentence: draws as many visitors a year as all of Turkey
transit:4.caveat: Turkey's count includes Turkish citizens living abroad who come to visit.
transit:4.note: New York City Tourism + Conventions annual report for 2025; the Turkish Statistical Institute's 2025 total visitor figure as reported by Daily Sabah. Turkey was the world's fourth most visited country. France's population (68.6 million) was the earlier comparison here.

land:9.sentence: has as many street trees as Toronto
land:9.caveat: New York City's count is from 2015-16; a new census is under way.
land:9.note: NYC Parks TreesCount 2015-2016; Toronto's street-tree inventory as compiled by the University of Toronto's School of Cities, because Toronto's own open-data page was retired. Both count municipally owned street trees and exclude park trees. Toronto has a third of New York City's population.

wealth:1.sentence: has as many jobs as the whole Chicago metropolitan area
wealth:1.caveat: Chicago's figure covers a three-state metropolitan area; New York City's covers the five boroughs.
wealth:1.note: Total nonfarm payroll jobs, July 2026, not seasonally adjusted, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics series for New York City and for the Chicago-Naperville-Elgin metropolitan area, both as published on FRED. Kuwait's population (4.90 million) was the earlier comparison here.

health:1.sentence: has as many people on food stamps as all of Illinois
health:1.caveat: Illinois's figure is four months earlier. Caseloads are falling in both places.
health:1.note: Human Resources Administration HRA Facts for July 2026; Illinois participation in March 2026 from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's state SNAP tables. Phoenix's population (1.67 million) was the earlier comparison here.

people:2.sentence: has as many foreign-born residents as Los Angeles County
people:2.caveat: Los Angeles County holds 9.8 million people to New York City's 8.5 million.
people:2.note: Both figures are the same Census Bureau table and year: American Community Survey 2024 one-year estimates, table B05002, variable B05002_013E ('Foreign-born'), queried for New York city and for Los Angeles County. This also confirms the City Planning Department's rounded 3.1 million. Armenia's population (3.10 million) was the earlier comparison here.

people:12.sentence: has as many residents 65 and older as Los Angeles County
people:12.note: Both figures are the same Census Bureau table and year: American Community Survey 2024 one-year estimates, subject table S0101, variable S0101_C01_030E ('65 years and over'), queried for New York city and for Los Angeles County. This is more current than the State Comptroller's 1.43 million for 2023, which the earlier version of this line used against Estonia's population.

people:11.sentence: had as many marathon finishers in 2025 as London
people:11.note: New York Road Runners' count for the Nov. 2, 2025 race, as reported by Running USA; London Marathon Events' own announcement for its April 2025 race. London set the world record for the largest marathon in April and New York took it back in November. Anfield's capacity was the earlier comparison here.

people:3.sentence: has as many public school students as all of Colorado
people:3.caveat: Colorado counts pre-K and charter schools; the city's figure is district schools, kindergarten through 12th grade.
people:3.note: Department of Education preliminary 2025-26 K-12 district enrollment, as reported by City Journal quoting the department; Colorado Department of Education's 2025-26 enrollment release. Counting New York City's charter schools and pre-K would put the city well above Colorado. North Dakota's population (799,358) was the earlier comparison here.

learning:5.sentence: sold as many Yankees tickets in 2025 as the Phillies sold in Philadelphia
learning:5.note: Both clubs' 2025 home attendance from the same ESPN season table, so the methodology matches. The Mets drew 3,182,052. Uruguay's population (3.39 million) was the earlier comparison here.

land:8.sentence: has as much parkland as El Paso
land:8.note: Both figures come from the Trust for Public Land's 2026 ParkScore index, which applies one definition of parkland to the 100 largest U.S. cities, so the two sides are measured identically. NYC Parks' own figure is 'more than 30,000 acres'. San Antonio (28,830 acres) was the next closest; San Diego, Houston, Los Angeles and Phoenix all have far more. The island of Jersey was the earlier comparison here.

money:10.sentence: has real estate worth as much as Mexico produces in a year
money:10.caveat: Department of Finance market values are the city's own estimates and lag sale prices.
money:10.note: Total market value of all city property on the fiscal 2027 tentative assessment roll, published Jan. 15, 2026; the International Monetary Fund's 2025 estimate of Mexico's nominal GDP. Spain's 2024 GDP was the earlier comparison, but the year gap was two years and its 2025 estimate is too high.
